title: Neon Drift
contributions: Built the arcade driving model and drift-scoring system, implemented the boost/chain combo loop, and wrote the replay-camera system used in trailers.
summary: A neon-soaked arcade racer about chaining perfect drifts. Built in 12 weeks as a vertical slice, with a focus on game-feel and a forgiving-but-deep scoring system.

title: Procedural Shader Toolkit
contributions: Designed a node-based authoring layer over raw shader graphs, wrote 30+ reusable function nodes, and built live hot-reload previews so artists iterate without recompiling.
summary: An artist-facing toolkit for authoring procedural materials without touching shader code. Cut the team's material-iteration time roughly in half during production.

title: Realtime Analytics Dashboard
contributions: Owned the streaming ingest pipeline and the WebSocket layer, designed the time-series aggregation schema, and built the front-end charting components from scratch.
summary: A live dashboard that ingests event streams and renders sub-second updates across thousands of concurrent sessions. Built to stay responsive under spiky, real-world load.

title: Co-op Puzzle Prototype
groupSize: Team of 2 — 1 engineer, 1 artist (me on both hats).
contributions: Prototyped the deterministic two-player physics, authored the stylized toon shader and outline pass, and built the level-flow tooling for rapid iteration.
summary: A bite-sized co-op puzzler about two players sharing one set of abilities. A game-jam prototype that doubled as a testbed for a custom stylized rendering pipeline.
